posts.text:
Twitter is a confusing place.

On a single post, I’ll get called an apologist/regime lobby and a war-mongering CIA/Mossad asset.

If both sides are mad, I’m probably doing something right...

The US/Israel launched the war in hopes of regime change or "at least the emergence of leaders more willing to bend to [their] interests... Instead, the void is being filled by radical new leaders who have shown little interest in political compromise..." wsj.com/world/middle-east/ir…

These are my fav type of posts because you know how warm and kind people are in their responses and how they're beaming with pride about their culture and country 🤍


Caitlin Doornbos (@CaitlinDoornbos)

Pakistani friends: Now that I'm staying in Pakistan for a few more days, any suggestions on what I should do and see in my off time? I'd love to take in some cultural experiences, but am still working so need to stay close to Islamabad.



— https://nitter.net/CaitlinDoornbos/status/204424443309

This is an ad for a mug store in Iran where young Iranians impersonate NPCs from Grand Theft Auto.

And folks wonder why the Iranian embassy’s trolling/ meme game is so strong. This is how plugged-in Iranians are when it comes to American pop culture and viral internet trends.

Video

That being said, I should note that some of that unity was again found briefly after the unprecedented massacre in January, as seen with the February 14 call to action by former Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi that amassed over a million diaspora protesters around the globe.
